items.prompt: Which macronutrient provides the most energy per gram?

options.label: Carbohydrate
Fat
Fibre
Protein

rubric: Fat provides about 9 kcal per gram, versus about 4 for protein and carbohydrate.
Distractors reflect the belief that protein or carbohydrate is most energy dense.

items.prompt: Which vitamin is the body able to make when skin is exposed to sunlight?

options.label: Vitamin D
Vitamin K
Vitamin B12
Vitamin C

rubric: Skin synthesises vitamin D with UVB exposure.
Vitamin C is a common wrong pick because it is linked with citrus and health.

items.prompt: Which mineral is a main component of bones and teeth?

options.label: Zinc
Iodine
Sodium
Calcium

rubric: Calcium is the main mineral in bones and teeth.
Sodium and others are minerals but not the main structural one.

items.prompt: What is the main role of protein in the diet?

options.label: Building and repairing body tissues
Providing the body's quickest source of fuel
Dissolving fat-soluble vitamins for absorption
Supplying water to keep the body hydrated

rubric: Protein supplies amino acids for building and repairing tissue.
Other options attribute roles of fat, water or nothing to protein.

items.prompt: Which unit is most commonly used on food labels to show energy content?

options.label: Litres per serving (L)
Milligrams per serving (mg)
Grams per serving (g)
Kilocalories (kcal)

rubric: Energy is shown in kcal or kJ.
Grams and milligrams measure mass of nutrients, not energy.

items.prompt: Which of the following are macronutrients? Select all that apply.

options.label: Carbohydrate
Iron
Protein
Fat
Vitamin A

rubric: Carbohydrate, protein and fat are macronutrients.
Vitamins and minerals are micronutrients needed in small amounts.

items.prompt: Sam is reading a food label and wants to find how much of the product's energy comes from sugars. Before calculating, Sam must recall how many kcal one gram of carbohydrate provides. What is the value?

options.label: About 7 kcal
About 9 kcal
About 2 kcal
About 4 kcal

rubric: Carbohydrate provides about 4 kcal per gram.
9 kcal is fat's value; 7 kcal is alcohol's.

items.prompt: Why is fibre recommended as part of a healthy diet?

options.label: It replaces the need for drinking enough water daily
It supports digestion and regular bowel movements
It is the body's fastest source of quick energy for muscles
It is broken down into amino acids that build muscle

rubric: Fibre aids digestion and bowel regularity.
Distractors confuse fibre with digestible energy or protein sources.

items.prompt: What happens to body weight over time if energy intake is consistently higher than energy expenditure?

options.label: Weight tends to fall as metabolism speeds up fully
Weight changes only if fat is eaten, not carbohydrate
Weight stays the same as the body burns the surplus
Weight tends to increase as extra energy is stored

rubric: A sustained surplus is stored, mainly as fat.
Distractors deny that any macronutrient surplus can be stored.

items.prompt: Which best explains the difference between water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins?

options.label: Water-soluble vitamins are stored in the liver for months, while fat-soluble ones must be eaten daily
Fat-soluble vitamins can be stored in body fat; water-soluble ones are mostly excreted
Water-soluble vitamins are stored in body fat, while fat-soluble ones are mostly excreted in urine
Fat-soluble vitamins come only from animal foods, while water-soluble ones come only from plants

rubric: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored; B and C are largely excreted.
Distractors reverse or blur the storage difference.

items.prompt: Which food would be classified as a good source of protein?

options.label: White sugar
Lemonade
Olive oil
Lentils

rubric: Lentils are rich in protein.
Sugar, oil and lemonade are mainly carbohydrate or fat.

items.prompt: Why does a food label list nutrients 'per 100 g' as well as per serving?

options.label: So the serving size shown is always the healthiest amount to eat
So the product weighs exactly 100 g in the pack it is sold in
So the vitamins listed are guaranteed to be absorbed by the body
So different products can be compared on the same basis

rubric: Per 100 g gives a standard basis for comparison.
Distractors misread it as pack weight or a recommended portion.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly describe the role of water in the body? Select all that apply.

options.label: It helps regulate body temperature
It is needed for removing waste via urine
It transports nutrients in the blood
It supplies about 4 kcal per gram

rubric: Water regulates temperature, transports nutrients and helps excrete waste.
Water contains no energy, so the kcal claim is wrong.

items.prompt: Priya skips fruit and vegetables for weeks and then notices her gums bleed easily and wounds heal slowly. A friend suggests a vitamin shortage. Which deficiency best explains these symptoms?

options.label: Vitamin C, needed for collagen formation
Vitamin A, needed for night vision
Iodine, needed for thyroid hormones
Vitamin D, needed for calcium absorption

rubric: Low vitamin C impairs collagen, causing bleeding gums and slow healing.
Other options are real deficiencies but with different symptoms.

items.prompt: Why does a meal rich in fibre often leave people feeling full for longer?

options.label: It is fully digested into amino acids, which signal the brain to stop eating
It slows digestion and adds bulk, so the stomach empties more gradually
It is absorbed as glucose quickly, so blood sugar rises and stays high
It carries more energy per gram than fat, so a little feels filling

rubric: Fibre adds bulk and slows stomach emptying, which prolongs fullness.
Distractors wrongly treat fibre as a digestible, energy-dense nutrient.

items.prompt: Vitamin K can be stored in the body's fat tissue, while vitamin C generally cannot. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.label: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, so it is stored in fat tissue; vitamin C is water-soluble and excess is mostly excreted
Vitamin K is water-soluble, so it dissolves into the blood and stays in circulation; vitamin C is fat-soluble and is excreted
Vitamin K is a mineral, so it is stored in bone; vitamin C is a vitamin, so it is not stored at all in the body
Both vitamins are fat-soluble, but the body absorbs vitamin C faster, so vitamin C does not build up in tissue

items.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the energy per gram of the three macronutrients?

options.label: Carbohydrate is highest, with fat and protein about equal
All three provide about the same energy per gram
Protein is highest, with carbohydrate and fat about equal
Fat is highest, with carbohydrate and protein about equal

rubric: Fat gives about 9 kcal per gram; carbohydrate and protein about 4.
Distractors reflect the belief that carbohydrate or protein is the most energy dense.

items.prompt: After a long walk in warm weather, a person's urine is dark yellow. What is the best interpretation?

options.label: Vitamin levels are low, so a supplement is the right first response
Too much water was drunk, so fluid should be cut back until it clears
Normal after exercise, since colour reflects only what was last eaten
Mild dehydration is likely, so drinking more fluid is a sensible step

rubric: Dark urine is a common sign of low hydration.
Distractors blame overhydration, vitamins or food rather than fluid status.

items.prompt: What is the main role of iron in the body?

options.label: It is the main fuel for the brain, so low intake causes fatigue
It forms part of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells
It hardens bones and teeth, so low intake raises fracture risk most
It balances fluid inside cells, so low intake causes muscle cramps

rubric: Iron is a component of haemoglobin and carries oxygen.
Distractors describe calcium, electrolytes and glucose roles.

items.prompt: Which foods are mainly sources of unsaturated fat? Select all that apply.

options.label: Butter
Avocado
Olive oil
Salmon
Coconut oil

rubric: Olive oil, oily fish and avocado are rich in unsaturated fats.
Butter and coconut oil are mostly saturated fat.

items.prompt: A friend eats a whole box of fat-free cookies every day, saying fat-free foods cannot cause weight gain. Which explanation of energy balance is most accurate?

options.label: Weight depends on nutrient type, so only fat grams count toward energy intake and sugar grams never do
Fat-free cookies are digested slowly, so they burn extra energy during processing and offset their calories
Fat-free foods still supply carbohydrate energy, so a regular surplus can be stored as fat
Fat-free foods can be eaten freely because only dietary fat can be stored as body fat in the body

rubric: Energy from any macronutrient counts toward balance, and surplus can be stored.
Distractors treat 'fat-free' as 'calorie-free' or as a special metabolic case.

items.prompt: A snack contains 20 g carbohydrate, 10 g protein and 5 g fat. Using 4, 4 and 9 kcal per gram, about how much energy does it provide?

options.label: 140 kcal
215 kcal
165 kcal
120 kcal

rubric: Other values come from using 4 kcal for fat or simply adding grams.

items.prompt: A cereal label states 8 g of sugar per 100 g. How much sugar is in a 150 g portion?

options.label: 8 g

rubric: Distractors ignore the portion size or scale it incorrectly.

items.prompt: A vegetarian wants to absorb more iron from a lentil meal. Which addition helps most?

options.label: A cup of strong tea, since its tannins help release iron from lentils
A slice of white bread, since refined grains bind iron for storage
A glass of milk, since its calcium boosts iron uptake from plant foods
A glass of orange juice, since vitamin C improves plant iron uptake

rubric: Vitamin C increases absorption of non-haem iron.
Tea and calcium reduce iron absorption; refined bread does not help.

items.prompt: Maria maintains her weight at 2,200 kcal a day and wants to lose about 0.5 kg a week (roughly 3,850 kcal per week). Which daily intake fits this goal?

options.label: 2,200 kcal
1,950 kcal
1,650 kcal
1,100 kcal

rubric: 1,950 is too small a deficit; 1,100 is too aggressive.

items.prompt: A 70 kg adult follows the standard recommendation of 0.8 g protein per kg of body weight per day. How many grams of protein is that?
rubric: Distractors misplace the decimal or ignore the per-kg rate.

items.prompt: A person eats white toast with jam and drinks orange juice for breakfast and wants more fibre. Which swaps apply this goal? Select all that apply.

options.label: Whole-grain toast instead of white toast
Oat porridge with berries instead of toast and jam
Whole orange instead of orange juice
Butter instead of jam
Sweetened fruit yogurt instead of juice

rubric: Whole grains, whole fruit and oats all add fibre.
Butter and sweetened yogurt contain no meaningful fibre.

items.prompt: Sam wants to limit added sugar. The ingredients on a granola bar read: oats, glucose syrup, raisins, honey, salt. Which conclusion applies the label rules correctly?

options.label: Raisins are the added sugar here, but honey does not count because it is natural
It has two added sugars, glucose syrup and honey, even though the word sugar is absent
It has no added sugar because the word sugar is not listed anywhere in the ingredients
Oats are listed first, so the bar must be mostly sugar by weight, with the syrup adding little

rubric: Added sugar appears under many names, including syrups and honey.
Distractors rely on the missing word 'sugar' or misread the ingredient order.

items.prompt: A snack label lists per serving: 12 g fat, 30 g carbohydrate and 8 g protein. Using standard energy values (fat 9, carbohydrate 4, protein 4 kcal per g), about how much energy is in one serving?

options.label: 290 kcal
224 kcal
200 kcal
260 kcal

rubric: 224 kcal comes from using 4 kcal/g for fat; 200 kcal comes from ignoring protein and miscounting.

items.prompt: A person needs 2,400 kcal a day and wants 20% of energy from protein (4 kcal per g). About how many grams of protein is that per day?
rubric: 480 g forgets to convert calories to grams; the others use wrong divisors.

items.prompt: A cereal label says 100 g contains 15 g of sugar. The serving size is 40 g, but you pour and weigh a 70 g bowl. About how much sugar are you eating?

options.label: 6 g

rubric: 70 g x 0.15 = 10.5 g of sugar.
15 g ignores the portion size; 6 g uses the label serving rather than the actual bowl.

items.prompt: A person maintains weight at 2,200 kcal a day and wants to lose about 0.5 kg per week. Assuming roughly 7,700 kcal per kg of body fat, which daily intake gives that deficit?

options.label: 1,950 kcal
1,450 kcal
1,100 kcal
1,650 kcal

rubric: 0.5 kg x 7,700 = 3,850 kcal per week, about 550 per day, so 2,200 - 550 = 1,650.
1,100 kcal applies a 1 kg per week deficit; 1,950 and 1,450 use arbitrary deficits.

items.prompt: A vegetarian is cooking a lentil stew and wants to maximise absorption of its non-heme iron. Which side dish best does this?

options.label: Whole-grain crackers, which are high in phytates
Black tea, which is high in tannins
Tomato and pepper salad, rich in vitamin C
Calcium-fortified milk, served at the same meal

rubric: Vitamin C converts non-heme iron into a form that is absorbed better.
Tannins, calcium and phytates all reduce non-heme iron absorption.

items.prompt: A person wants to raise daily fibre intake without changing the number of meals. Which swaps would be expected to increase fibre? Select all that apply.

options.label: Replace white rice with cooked barley
Replace whole-grain bread with white bread
Replace half the mince in chilli with beans
Replace fruit juice with the same fruit eaten whole

rubric: Barley, whole fruit with skin and pulp, and beans all add fibre.
White bread has less fibre than whole-grain bread, so that swap lowers intake.

items.prompt: An athlete weighing 70 kg aims for 1.6 g of protein per kg body weight daily. Planned meals provide 90 g. She wants one snack to cover the remaining gap as closely as possible. Which snack fits best?

options.label: 250 g yogurt with 9 g protein per 100 g
Four boiled eggs at 6 g protein each, peeled
30 g almonds with about 6 g protein per portion
One banana with about 1 g protein per fruit

rubric: Target is 70 x 1.6 = 112 g, a gap of 22 g; 250 g yogurt gives about 22.5 g.
The eggs, almonds and banana fall well short because the gap was not calculated.

items.prompt: A man starts a very low-carbohydrate diet and loses 2 kg in the first week. He concludes he has lost 2 kg of body fat. Which analysis is most accurate?

options.label: Much of the early loss is likely water released with depleted glycogen
The scale is unreliable, so no change in weight actually occurred
Fat loss is always about 2 kg when carbohydrate is cut sharply
The loss must be muscle, since fat cannot be lost within a week

rubric: Glycogen is stored with water, so early low-carbohydrate loss is largely water.
Other options wrongly attribute the whole change to fat, muscle or measurement error.

items.prompt: A cereal's ingredient list begins: oats, sugar, honey, glucose syrup, wheat flour. The front says 'contains whole grain oats'. What does the list reveal?

options.label: Honey is a natural sugar, so it should not be counted as sugar in the list
Glucose syrup is a fibre ingredient, so it offsets the sugars listed before it
Several sugar sources are listed separately, so total sugar may exceed oats
Oats are listed first, so the product must be low in added sugar overall

rubric: Splitting sugar into sugar, honey and glucose syrup hides that combined sugars may outweigh oats.
Honey and syrups count as free sugars; glucose syrup is not fibre.

items.prompt: A strict vegan who takes no supplements reports fatigue, pale skin and tingling in the hands and feet. Which deficiency best explains this pattern, given the diet?

options.label: Vitamin C, which only citrus fruit supplies
Vitamin K, which vegans rarely get from leafy greens
Vitamin B12, which plant foods do not reliably supply
Vitamin A, which is found only in orange produce and animal foods

rubric: B12 is found almost only in animal foods, and deficiency causes anaemia and nerve symptoms.
The other vitamins are plentiful in plant foods and do not cause this combination.

items.prompt: A survey finds that people who eat breakfast weigh less than those who skip it, and a magazine says breakfast causes weight loss. What is the main flaw in that reasoning?

options.label: Confounding: breakfast eaters may differ in other habits that affect weight
Reverse causation: people who weigh less may be more likely to eat breakfast
Sampling error: a survey of this kind usually has too few people to show any link
Measurement bias: self-reported weight tends to be underreported by breakfast eaters

rubric: An observational link can be driven by other habits such as activity, sleep and overall diet, so it does not show causation.
The other options give unsupported or overbroad objections.

items.prompt: A woman logs 1,600 kcal a day and her weight has not changed for six weeks, though her estimated needs are 2,000 kcal. Which explanation should be checked first?

options.label: Water has no effect on scale weight in a deficit
Protein in her diet cannot be used for energy at all
Her metabolism has stopped completely because of the low intake
Under-recording of oils, drinks, snacks and portion sizes in her log

rubric: Self-reported intake is commonly underestimated, especially cooking fats, drinks and portions.
Metabolism does not stop; the other options are false statements about physiology.

items.prompt: Two adults of the same age and height eat identical diets, but one gains weight while the other maintains. Which factors could explain a difference in their energy needs? Select all that apply.

options.label: Difference in lean body mass, which changes resting energy expenditure
Difference in training or activity level, which changes energy used in exercise
Difference in the proportion of calories eaten at night, which shifts total daily energy needs
Difference in everyday non-exercise movement, such as fidgeting, standing and walking
Difference in the protein share of the diet, which changes the energy each person needs

rubric: Lean mass, non-exercise movement and exercise all change total daily energy expenditure.
Hair colour and cuisine preference do not alter energy needs.

items.prompt: A runner drinks large amounts of plain water during a 4-hour hot race, with no food or salty drinks. Near the end she has a headache, nausea and bloating, and she has gained 1 kg since the start. Which cause best fits this pattern?

options.label: Vitamin C deficiency from sweating over several hours
Low sodium in the blood from excess plain water intake
Dehydration, because weight rises when fluid is low
Glycogen depletion, which causes weight gain and bloating

rubric: Weight gain plus nausea and headache after heavy plain water intake suggests dilution of blood sodium (hyponatraemia).
Dehydration would show weight loss, and glycogen or vitamin C explanations do not match the weight gain.

items.prompt: An endurance athlete eats spinach, fortified cereal and only small portions of meat, and drinks tea with meals. Her iron intake looks adequate on paper, yet ferritin is low. Which analysis best explains the gap?

options.label: Vitamin C in the meal competes with iron for transporters, so absorption drops whenever fruit is eaten with it
Tannins in tea and phytates in cereal and spinach bind non-heme iron, cutting how much of it is absorbed
Heme iron from the small meat portions blocks uptake of the plant iron, leaving total absorption unchanged
Fortified cereal iron is chemically unabsorbable, so it counts as zero toward the daily requirement

rubric: Polyphenols and phytates inhibit non-heme iron absorption, so intake figures overstate what is absorbed.
Vitamin C enhances rather than blocks non-heme iron absorption; heme iron does not block plant iron.

items.prompt: A person who logs exactly 2,000 kcal a day, matching maintenance, weighs 1.4 kg heavier the morning after a salty, high-carbohydrate restaurant meal. Which analysis of the gain is best?

options.label: Sodium raises metabolic rate sharply, so weight should have dropped and the scale reading must be faulty
The meal exceeded maintenance by roughly 10,000 kcal, so the gain must be mostly newly stored body fat
Carbohydrate converts to fat within hours at a fixed rate, so the scale is showing fat from that single meal
Extra sodium and stored glycogen hold water, so most of the gain is fluid rather than newly stored body fat

rubric: Sodium and glycogen each bind water, so short-term jumps reflect fluid; 1.4 kg of fat would need about 10,000 kcal surplus.
Distractors treat any overnight scale change as fat gain or deny the water effect.

items.prompt: Cooking lentils with rice is said to improve overall protein quality compared with eating either alone. Which analysis explains why?

options.label: Rice is low in lysine and lentils are low in methionine, so each supplies the amino acid the other lacks
Cooking them together destroys antinutrients in both foods, which raises the amino acid content of each
Lentils and rice together supply more total grams of protein, and gram totals alone set a protein quality score
Rice supplies essential fatty acids that let the body convert lentil protein into its missing amino acids

rubric: Complementary limiting amino acids (lysine in cereals, methionine in legumes) make the combination more complete.
Distractors confuse quantity with quality or invent amino acid conversion from fatty acids.

items.prompt: A man on a very low-fat diet takes a vitamin D capsule each morning on an empty stomach, yet his blood level stays low. Which cause is most likely?

options.label: Low fat intake blocks skin synthesis of vitamin D, which is the only route by which the body gets it, so capsules cannot raise levels
Vitamin D is water-soluble and is flushed out in urine, so a dose taken while fasting is lost within a few hours
Vitamin D is fat-soluble, so with almost no dietary fat to prompt bile release, capsule absorption is poor
Supplemental vitamin D is absorbed only alongside calcium-rich foods, and the amount of dietary fat has no effect on it

rubric: Fat-soluble vitamins need dietary fat and bile for micelle formation and absorption.
Distractors misclassify vitamin D's solubility or invent calcium dependence.

items.prompt: A bottle of 100% fruit juice says 'no added sugar' but lists 24 g sugars per cup. A shopper claims it is nutritionally equal to eating whole fruit with the same sugar. Which analysis identifies the flaw?

options.label: Juicing strips most fibre and makes sugar fast to drink, so fullness is lower and the sugar counts as free sugar
Fructose in whole fruit is metabolised differently from juice fructose, so juice sugar is chemically more harmful
A label saying 'no added sugar' must be false whenever sugars are listed, so the claim is illegal
Whole fruit and juice contain equal fibre, so the only difference is preservatives in the bottle

rubric: Juicing releases intrinsic sugars and removes fibre structure, reducing satiety and speeding intake.
Distractors invent chemical differences or misread what 'no added sugar' means.

items.prompt: A dieter logs a 500 kcal daily deficit for three weeks but loses far less than predicted. Which factors could explain the gap? Select all that apply.

options.label: Water retention can mask fat lost over a few weeks, hiding change on the scale
Daily movement outside exercise often falls in a deficit, shrinking the real gap
Intake is under-reported, as portions and extras are often missed in logs
Fat holds 9 kcal per gram, so a deficit only counts if it comes entirely from dietary fat
Protein has no thermic effect, so a high-protein diet adds extra usable calories

rubric: Under-reporting, lower non-exercise activity and fluid shifts commonly shrink or hide the expected loss.
The fat-only and protein-thermic claims misunderstand how energy balance works.

items.prompt: A recreational marathon runner drinks about 1 L of plain water each hour during a slow 5-hour race, sipping at every aid station. At the finish she has headache, nausea and puffy hands, and weighs 2 kg more than at the start. Which diagnosis best explains her state?

options.label: Glycogen depletion: running out of carbohydrate causes puffiness and a rise in body weight
Dehydration: fluid losses exceeded intake, concentrating her blood and causing headache and nausea
Dilutional hyponatremia: fluid intake exceeded sweat losses, lowering her blood sodium concentration
Hypernatremia: sweat sodium loss raised her blood sodium concentration and caused swelling

rubric: Weight gain and swelling after heavy plain-water intake point to overhydration and diluted blood sodium.
Dehydration would show weight loss; sweat sodium loss lowers, not raises, blood sodium.

items.prompt: A client wants a breakfast that keeps her full until lunch. Criteria: under 400 kcal, at least 25 g protein and at least 5 g fibre. Which option meets all three?

options.label: Two slices of white toast with jam and a latte: 340 kcal, 12 g protein, 2 g fibre
Three-egg cheese omelette with buttered toast: 620 kcal, 33 g protein, 3 g fibre
Large bran muffin and orange juice: 480 kcal, 8 g protein, 4 g fibre
Greek yogurt with berries and a little oats: 330 kcal, 28 g protein, 6 g fibre

rubric: Only the yogurt bowl meets calorie, protein and fibre criteria together.
Each distractor satisfies at most one criterion and looks healthy for another reason.

items.prompt: A company sells a 5-day juice-only 'detox' claiming to flush toxins. Judged against physiology and evidence, which critique is strongest?

options.label: It is weak: the liver and kidneys already clear waste, and juice-only lacks protein, with no proof it removes extra toxins
It is sound: the liver and kidneys can only clear built-up waste when the gut is rested on liquids for several days in a row
It is weak only because it lasts five days; trials show juice cleanses of a month or more do measurably clear stored toxins
It is sound: sugars in juice chemically bind toxins in the gut, and the bound toxins then leave the body in the stool

rubric: Detox claims lack evidence; organs handle waste and a juice-only plan is low in protein.
Distractors endorse unsupported mechanisms or imply longer cleanses work.

items.prompt: A vegan asks how to secure vitamin B12 reliably at low cost. Criteria: dependable supply, low expense, and avoiding silent long-term deficiency. Which advice is best?

options.label: Eat large servings of leafy greens and seaweed daily, as these provide bioavailable B12 in amounts that prevent deficiency over time
Take a routine B12 supplement or eat fortified foods, since plant foods lack reliable B12 and deficiency is silent
Wait for symptoms before supplementing, since liver stores of B12 last a lifetime without topping up and symptoms appear early enough to treat
Eat unfortified nutritional yeast and fermented soy, since fermentation by bacteria yields active B12 in dependable amounts that meet needs

rubric: Supplements or fortified foods are cheap and dependable; unfortified plant foods are not reliable sources.
Distractors rely on unreliable sources or delay action despite silent deficiency risk.

items.prompt: A cohort study finds people who eat more red meat have more heart disease. Which limitation matters most when judging whether meat itself causes the disease?

options.label: Confounding: heavy meat eaters may also smoke, exercise less and eat fewer vegetables, so the link may not be causal
Any human diet association is invalid unless a trial follows participants for their entire lifespan
Food questionnaires measure intake precisely, so the main limitation is too few cuts of meat being included
Cohort studies cannot record disease outcomes, only food intake, so no link could legitimately be reported

rubric: Observational data cannot rule out confounding from correlated lifestyle behaviours.
Distractors overstate cohort limits or dismiss all non-lifelong evidence.

items.prompt: Evidence shows matched-calorie, matched-protein low-carb and low-fat plans produce similar fat loss. A client who loves bread and pasta needs a plan sustainable for 12 months with protein at 1.6 g/kg. Which recommendation is best?

options.label: Choose whichever plan has fewer calories, even if protein falls below target, because deficit size matters more than protein for fat loss
Choose low-carb, because lower insulin levels give it a fat loss advantage even when calories and protein are matched
A lower-fat plan meeting the protein target, since results are similar and adherence to preferred foods drives sustainability
Alternate the two plans weekly, because switching prevents metabolic adaptation and so keeps fat loss higher than either plan alone

rubric: With equal outcomes, adherence and meeting stated protein criteria should drive the choice.
Distractors claim unsupported metabolic advantages or ignore the stated protein constraint.

items.prompt: You are judging a snack bar marketed as 'high protein'. Which are sound criteria for evaluating the claim? Select all that apply.

options.label: Whether the word 'protein' is printed first on the front, which signals quality
Added sugar and saturated fat per bar, which can offset the protein benefit
Protein grams relative to the bar's calories, not the front-of-pack claim
Whether it uses sugar alcohols, which guarantees zero calories from sweeteners
Whether the serving size matches what people actually eat

rubric: Protein density, offsetting nutrients and realistic servings are legitimate label-based criteria.
Front-of-pack wording and the zero-calorie sugar alcohol idea are marketing or factual errors.

items.prompt: A dietitian advises a client with high blood pressure, normal kidney function and a tight grocery budget. Criteria: cut sodium meaningfully, keep potassium intake adequate, and stay affordable. Which plan is best?

options.label: Cook from basic ingredients, rinse canned beans, and add potassium-rich vegetables, cutting sodium at processed sources
Take a high-dose potassium supplement daily and keep current meals unchanged, since potassium fully cancels out the effect of sodium on pressure
Cut fluids sharply to lower blood volume and pressure, since total water intake matters more than dietary sodium for blood pressure control
Remove the table salt shaker only and keep eating processed foods, since the shaker supplies most of the sodium in a typical diet

rubric: Most sodium comes from processed foods; cooking from basics and adding potassium-rich produce is cheap and effective.
Distractors target the shaker only, rely on supplements, or restrict fluids without basis.

items.prompt: A coach claims six small meals a day beat three larger ones for fat loss because frequent eating 'stokes the metabolism'. Which critique is best supported by controlled evidence?

options.label: Meal frequency matters only for people under 60 kg, since larger bodies burn the same calories whatever the timing of meals
Fewer, larger meals raise the thermic effect per meal enough that three meals clearly beat six for fat loss at equal intake
Thermic effect depends on total energy and macronutrients eaten, so at equal intake meal frequency barely changes expenditure
Each small meal lifts resting metabolic rate, but the extra insulin released cancels the gain and so blocks fat loss entirely

rubric: Diet-induced thermogenesis scales with total intake, so splitting the same food into more meals changes little.
Distractors invent a frequency effect in either direction or restrict it to a body-size group.

items.prompt: A large cohort study finds that people eating the most processed meat have higher colorectal cancer rates. Judged by causal-inference criteria, which limitation most weakens the claim that the meat itself caused the excess?

options.label: Healthy-user confounding and error-prone food frequency questionnaires leave residual bias that adjustment cannot fully remove
Relative risks are meaningless unless absolute risk in the exposed group exceeds 50 percent, which rules out the finding
A very large sample makes any association statistically unreliable, so the result is most likely due to chance alone
Cohort designs cannot record diet at all, so the researchers cannot know who was actually exposed to processed meat

rubric: Observational diet studies suffer from correlated lifestyle confounders and noisy self-reported intake, limiting causal claims.
Distractors misstate what sample size, cohort design and relative risk imply.

items.prompt: Cereal A's label lists 4 g added sugar per 40 g serving; Cereal B lists 4 g added sugar per 30 g serving. A client usually eats 60 g of whichever she buys. Judged on added sugar at her real portion, which is the better choice?

options.label: Cereal A, because 60 g gives about 6 g added sugar versus about 8 g for B, once scaled to her actual portion
Cereal B, because 4 g per 30 g is the lower figure once both are converted to a per-gram basis
Cereal B, because its smaller serving suggests a leaner recipe, and both labels show the same 4 g of added sugar
Neither differs, because per-serving figures are standardised so they compare directly across brands and portions

rubric: Scaling per-serving values to the real portion gives A about 6 g and B about 8 g, so A is better.
Distractors assume identical serving sizes or reverse the per-gram comparison.

items.prompt: A 75 kg vegan strength athlete wants to maximise muscle gain with practical meals. Which approach is best justified by current evidence on plant protein?

options.label: Use a branched-chain amino acid supplement, since plant protein cannot supply enough leucine to drive muscle protein synthesis at any intake
Pair specific complementary proteins inside every single meal, since the body cannot pool amino acids across the day and so wastes incomplete meals
Stay at 0.8 g/kg protein, since plant protein is digested more completely than animal protein and so needs no extra intake for training
Eat about 1.6 to 2.0 g/kg protein across meals from soy, legumes and grains, offsetting lower digestibility and leucine

rubric: Higher total intake from varied plant sources compensates for lower digestibility and leucine density.
Distractors reflect the strict meal-by-meal complementation myth, a supplement fix, or a false digestibility claim.

items.prompt: A runner plans a 5-hour trail race and intends to drink a fixed 1 litre of plain water every hour 'to stay ahead of dehydration'. Which critique is most valid?

options.label: A fixed high intake of low-sodium fluid risks dilutional hyponatremia; thirst-guided drinking with sodium is safer
Losing 1 to 2 percent of body mass impairs performance and raises risk, so fluid intake should match sweat losses closely
Fluid needs rise with duration and heat, so 1 litre per hour is probably too low for a 5-hour effort in warm conditions
Plain water is absorbed more slowly than carbohydrate drinks during exercise, so sports drinks protect performance better

rubric: Overdrinking low-sodium fluid over hours can cause exercise-associated hyponatremia; thirst-guided drinking with sodium is safer.
Distractors treat mild dehydration as dangerous or assume fixed high volumes are always needed.

items.prompt: Evaluate claims about ketogenic diets for fat loss. Which are well supported by current evidence? Select all that apply.

options.label: In tightly controlled feeding studies with matched calories and protein, fat loss is not markedly greater than on higher-carbohydrate diets
Ketosis makes surplus dietary energy unusable, so calorie intake stops affecting body weight
Much of the first-week weight drop reflects lost glycogen and its bound water rather than body fat
Reduced appetite in some people may lower energy intake, a plausible practical benefit worth weighing
Because carbohydrate is nearly absent, the body must break down muscle to supply all of its glucose needs

rubric: Early water loss, similar fat loss under matched conditions, and possible appetite effects are supported.
Obligatory muscle breakdown and 'calories stop counting' are common misconceptions; gluconeogenesis and ketones cover needs and energy balance still applies.

items.prompt: A 62-year-old man on stable warfarin plans to start a daily kale and spinach smoothie after reading that greens are healthy. His anticoagulation clinic has not been told. Weighing risk and benefit, what is the best advice?

options.label: Start the smoothie now and let the drug adapt, since warfarin dosing self-adjusts to changes in diet
Avoid all leafy greens permanently, since vitamin K opposes warfarin and any intake makes the drug unsafe
Add it only on low-activity days, since exercise level rather than vitamin K governs warfarin response
Keep vitamin K intake consistent from day to day and tell the clinic first so dosing can be matched to it

rubric: Warfarin control depends on steady vitamin K intake; greens are beneficial if consistent and the clinic is informed.
Distractors recommend blanket avoidance, ignoring interaction, or a wrong mechanism.

items.prompt: Design a meal for a 70 kg runner eating 3 hours before a 10 km race. Constraints: about 2 g/kg carbohydrate, low fat and fibre to limit GI upset, modest protein, familiar foods. Which meal meets all of them?

options.label: Large raw salad with grilled chicken and olive oil, giving roughly 40 g carbohydrate and a very light stomach
White rice (about 2 cups cooked) with a banana, honey and a little egg white, giving roughly 135 g carbohydrate
Bacon and cheese omelette with buttered toast, giving roughly 140 g carbohydrate and plenty of satisfying protein
Bran cereal with milk, an apple and a handful of almonds, giving roughly 140 g carbohydrate in a familiar meal

rubric: Rice, banana and honey supply about 2 g/kg carbohydrate with little fat or fibre.
Distractors break the low-fibre, low-fat or carbohydrate-target constraint.

items.prompt: A dietitian drafts a vegan plan: lentils, tofu, whole grains, fortified soy milk, nuts, seeds and leafy greens. Which missing element most needs adding for the plan to meet every nutrient need?

options.label: Pairing complementary proteins at each meal, since single plant foods usually lack enough of some essential amino acids
A reliable vitamin B12 source such as a supplement or B12-fortified foods, since plants do not supply it dependably
A heme iron source such as a daily iron supplement, since non-heme iron from plants is absorbed poorly and may fall short
Vitamin D from sun-exposed mushrooms alone, since this plan has no vitamin D source and bone health depends on it

rubric: Vitamin B12 has no dependable unfortified plant source, so a supplement or fortified food is essential.
Distractors rely on outdated protein-combining, a false iron absorption claim, or a false claim that greens lack vitamin C.

items.prompt: A client who feels better off gluten wants to know whether she has non-coeliac gluten sensitivity. Constraints: coeliac disease must be excluded first and expectation bias minimised. Which design is best?

options.label: Run coeliac serology while she is still eating gluten, then a blinded placebo-controlled gluten challenge after a gluten-free baseline
Reintroduce gluten openly after four weeks off and record symptoms in a daily diary, since blinding adds little value when the client is motivated to report accurately
Do a skin-prick wheat allergy test alone, since a negative IgE result also rules out coeliac disease and non-coeliac gluten sensitivity
Go gluten-free for four weeks, then run coeliac serology to see whether antibody levels have returned to normal and confirm the diagnosis

rubric: Serology needs ongoing gluten intake, and a blinded challenge separates true reactions from nocebo effects.
Distractors test coeliac disease after gluten removal, skip blinding, or use an allergy test for the wrong condition.

items.prompt: An adult with hypertension and normal kidney function has a tight food budget and gets most sodium from packaged and restaurant food. Which plan meets all: sodium under 2,300 mg, adequate potassium, affordable?

options.label: Cook more from basic ingredients, season with herbs and acid, and add beans, potatoes and vegetables for potassium
Swap fresh produce for low-sodium canned soups and potassium pills, which avoids cooking costs while cutting sodium sharply
Cut sodium below 500 mg a day, because blood pressure falls in direct proportion with no floor and no downside
Remove the salt shaker and switch to sea salt, since most sodium comes from table salt and sea salt has far less of it

rubric: Most sodium comes from processed food, so home cooking with potassium-rich staples meets all constraints cheaply.
Distractors target table salt only, expensive substitutes, or an extreme cut.

items.prompt: An 80 kg man with maintenance intake near 2,600 kcal wants to lose about 0.5 kg per week while keeping muscle and sticking with the plan. Which plan meets all constraints?

options.label: Eat about 2,050 kcal with protein near 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg and resistance training about three times weekly
Eat 1,200 kcal daily with light walking, since the faster the deficit the better muscle is preserved
Eat 2,600 kcal and add 90 minutes of running daily, so that no change to food intake is needed at all
Eat about 2,050 kcal with 0.8 g/kg protein and cardio only, since extra protein beyond that is stored as fat

rubric: A deficit of about 550 kcal per day, high protein and resistance training suit the loss rate and muscle retention.
Distractors use an extreme deficit, low protein without lifting, or an unsustainable exercise-only approach.

items.prompt: A vegetarian has low ferritin. Design meal additions that raise non-heme iron absorption. Which fit the goal? Select all that apply.

options.label: Include a vitamin C source such as peppers or citrus alongside iron-rich meals
Drink tea or coffee with meals, since the polyphenols bind iron into a form that is easier to absorb
Soak, sprout or ferment legumes and grains to reduce their phytate content
Take a calcium supplement with the main iron-rich meal to boost iron uptake
Keep tea and coffee at least an hour away from iron-rich meals

rubric: Vitamin C, phytate reduction and separating polyphenol drinks all improve non-heme iron absorption.
Tea with meals and calcium with iron both inhibit absorption.

items.prompt: A 78-year-old man has lost 5 kg in three months, has poor appetite and ill-fitting dentures, and eats about 1,400 kcal and 45 g protein daily (needs about 2,000 kcal and 80 g protein). Which plan best meets his energy, protein and chewing constraints?

options.label: Switch to low-fat, high-fibre foods and raw vegetables to protect his heart and make small portions feel filling
Three soft, full-fat meals plus fortified milk, nut-butter and Greek yogurt snacks between them to add energy and protein
Replace most meals with clear broth and diet fluids to ease chewing and reduce the load on a poor appetite and his weak swallow
Keep three larger standard meals with no snacks between them, since eating between meals suppresses appetite at the next mealtime

rubric: Soft, energy- and protein-dense small feeds close the gap without demanding chewing or large volumes.
Distractors cut energy density, ignore chewing limits or replace nutrients with low-energy fluids.
